hypothesis: Interleaving memory policy only for the copy/hash child may distribute destination page-cache allocation across the two Iris NUMA nodes and alter a short solver screen, even when the measured launcher-parent memory policy and all native runtime settings are held constant.

mechanism_evidence.observation: Each inherited-preparation arm showed approximately +9.78 GiB FilePages on node 1 and +0 on node 0; each interleaved-preparation arm showed approximately +4.89 GiB on each node.
mechanism_evidence.limit: Cumulative node-wide counters are not process-attributed page placement and do not establish a solver-performance effect.

control: Same accepted Scotch source, same runtime, solver launch, physics, 20-step screen, sampler, and observed inherited launcher-parent policy in all arms.
treatment: Copy/hash child inherited policy versus child-only numactl --interleave=all.
